transcript.text: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out? It's still under guarantee so I want to report it before it dies completely.

It is unlikely to be the motor itself, especially at four months old. The symptoms you describe—louder noise and faster battery drain on rugs—are classic signs of the motor working harder because it cannot pull enough air through the carpet fibres. When airflow drops, the laser sensor can also behave erratically (the screen going up and down), as the system struggles to maintain its calibration or power levels under load. However, this is often caused by something simple restricting that airflow further:
1. Clogged filters: If they are dirty or slightly damp, they choke the motor on high-suction surfaces like rugs.
2. A blockage: Something stuck in the wand or floorhead will cause exactly this behaviour. Please check if the filters are clean and dry, and ensure there is no debris blocking the airway. Let me know what you find.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

I washed the filter at the back last month and left it to dry for a full day. I've also looked down the wand and it's clear. There's no burning smell, heat or sparks, and nothing looks swollen. It still picks up well, it just gets louder on the rug. What should I check next?

Since the filters are clean and dry and the wand is clear, the next most likely cause for increased noise and battery drain on rugs is a restriction in the floorhead itself. When suction hits a rug, it pulls more air through the brush bar; if hair or thread has wrapped around the roller ends, it creates drag that makes the motor work much harder (louder noise) and drains the battery faster. Please turn the vacuum off, remove the battery, flip the floorhead over, and spin the brush bar by hand. Does it spin freely, or is there resistance? Also check for any hair wrapped around the ends of the roller. If the brush bar spins freely and is clean, this points more towards an internal issue with the laser sensor calibration or a minor blockage deeper in the bin inlet that isn't visible from the wand. Let me know what you find with the brush bar.

I've checked the brush bar and it's clean, no hair wrapped round it, the comb part seems to be doing its job. I haven't spun it by hand though, so I can't say about resistance. I'm using the Digital Motorbar head, if that helps. I won't be opening up the motor body or taking any screws out as it's under guarantee.

The next most likely cause is that the floorhead's own internal filter (a small white mesh piece inside the bin inlet area) is clogged with fine dust. When you move onto a rug, the suction increases to pull air through the carpet; if this secondary filter is blocked, the motor has to work much harder (louder noise) and drains the battery faster. Please remove that small internal filter from the floorhead, check it, and wash it in cold water if dirty. Let it dry fully for 24 hours before putting it back. If that doesn't fix it, the erratic screen behaviour combined with the load issue suggests a fault in the laser sensor module or its wiring within the head itself. Given the vacuum is only four months old and under guarantee, I would recommend arranging a repair or replacement through Dyson once you've tried cleaning that internal filter.
